title: Undo and redo text buffer
instructions:
Implement `TextBuffer` in `text_buffer.py` using undo and redo stacks.

## Files
- `text_buffer.py`

API:
- `TextBuffer(text: str = "")` starts with the given text and empty history.
- Read-only property `text: str` gives the current text.
- `insert(position: int, text: str) -> None` inserts before that character;
  positions from 0 through the current length are valid.
- `delete(start: int, end: int) -> str` removes and returns the half-open
  slice `[start, end)`. Require `0 <= start <= end <= len(text)`.
- Invalid insert positions or delete intervals raise `IndexError` without
  changing text or either history stack. Validate even an empty insertion.
- `undo() -> bool` undoes one changing edit, returning True; returns False
  without changes if no edit is available.
- `redo() -> bool` reapplies one undone edit, returning True; returns False
  without changes if unavailable.

Each changing insertion or deletion is one history entry and clears redo.
Empty insertions and empty deletions create no history and preserve redo.
The initial text is not a history entry. Indexes count Python string characters,
including Unicode. Arguments have the annotated types; other type validation
is not required. Do not expose mutable history as part of the public API.
